records.title: VeriFactu records
records.search: Search invoice, issuer or tax ID…
records.empty: No records yet. Every invoice you issue is sealed and listed here.
records.noResultsMessage: Nothing matches the search or the filters.
records.loadError: The records could not be loaded

detail.title: Record {number}
detail.xmlPending: The XML is built when the producer's details arrive from your ERPlora account.
detail.waitingWhen: It goes out by itself with the next pass, in order, and declared as late if it failed before. You do not have to do anything.
detail.rejectedHelp: If the invoice itself is wrong (a customer's tax ID the AEAT does not know, an amount), rectify it in Invoicing. If not (the chain after restoring a backup, a fault of ours), correct the record.
detail.correctMessage: A new record of the same invoice, read again, is sealed as a correction and goes to the AEAT. The rejected one is kept as it is.
detail.correctDone: Correction of {number} sealed: it goes out with the next pass.
detail.cancelNote: The AEAT will be told this invoice was issued by error. A refund or a correction is never this: it is a rectifying invoice in Invoicing. The invoice stays in Invoicing.
detail.cancelDone: Cancellation of {number} sealed: it goes out with the next pass.
detail.reasonRequired: Write why the invoice was issued by error.

contingency.processFailed: The queue could not be processed
contingency.empty: Queue empty: everything is in the AEAT.
contingency.loadError: The queue could not be loaded
contingency.retried: {number} goes out with the next pass.

events.title: Audit events
events.loadError: The events could not be loaded

recovery.title: Chain recovery
recovery.scope: This recomputes the SHA-256 fingerprints and verifies the chaining. It does not re-audit the amounts: the base, the tax and the total are taken as the invoice declared them.
recovery.manualHint: Paste the last fingerprint (64 hex) of your previous application, with its invoice number and date, to continue the same chain.
recovery.hashInvalid: The fingerprint must be 64 hexadecimal characters
recovery.confirmAeatTitle: Recover the chain from the AEAT
recovery.confirmAeatMessage: Local continuity will be rebuilt from the latest record available at the AEAT. Verify the issuer tax ID before continuing.
recovery.confirmManualTitle: Continue the chain from an external fingerprint
recovery.confirmManualMessage: The fingerprint given will be the predecessor of the next fiscal record. Use this only during a migration and with the data of the last record of the previous application.
recovery.failed: The operation could not be done

config.title: VeriFactu configuration

grant.none: Not signed. Your business cannot go live through ERPlora until you sign it.
grant.submitted: Under review since {date}. We let you know by email.
grant.approved: Approved on {date}: ERPlora can file on your behalf.
grant.returned: Returned on {date}. Correct what is said and send it again.

config.expiresSoon: Expires in {n} days: upload the renewed one here.
config.expired: The certificate has expired. Upload a valid one to send to the AEAT.
config.keysNote: The certificate and its password are kept encrypted in this Hub and only travel to ERPlora's gateway when sending to the AEAT; they are never shown again.
config.notSynced: Your ERPlora account has not sent this yet.
config.loadError: The configuration could not be loaded
config.certHint: Upload the business's certificate (.p12 or .pfx) with its password. It must belong to Invoicing's issuer.
config.tooLarge: The file is larger than 1 MB: it is not a certificate.
config.unreadableFile: The file could not be read.
config.uploadFailed: The certificate could not be uploaded.
config.removeMessage: With «My certificate» as the route, records wait in the queue until you upload another one or choose «ERPlora files for you».
config.removeFailed: The certificate could not be removed.

settings.title: VeriFactu settings
settings.ownOn: You file directly with the tax agency using your business certificate, uploaded in Configuration → My certificate.
settings.ownOff: ERPlora files your billing records with the tax agency on your behalf, with its own seal. You do not need a certificate.
settings.routeOwn: Done: from now on you send with your own certificate.
settings.routeErplora: Done: from now on ERPlora files on your behalf.
settings.goLiveHint: Your invoices go to the AEAT's test environment. When everything is ready, go live.
settings.goLiveTitle: Send your invoices to the AEAT for real?
settings.goLiveMessage: From now on every record goes to the real AEAT. As soon as the first one is sealed you can no longer go back to testing.
settings.wentLive: Your business is live: records now go to the real AEAT.
settings.productionClosed: Going live is not open on this server yet: ERPlora opens it when the real submission is ready.
settings.backHint: No record has been sealed in production yet, so you can still go back to testing.
settings.backTitle: Go back to the test environment?
settings.backMessage: Records will go to the AEAT's test environment again and will not count before the tax agency.
settings.backDone: Your business is back in the test environment.
settings.oneWay: Your business already has records in production, so it cannot go back to testing.
settings.testHint: Checks everything needed to send, without presenting anything to the AEAT: a filed record cannot be undone.
settings.testTestingOnly: The test invoice is only for the test environment.
settings.testCreated: Test invoice {number} created: its record is in Records.
settings.declarationDesc: The declaration ERPlora signs for the version of the system you are running, and the identifying data every record carries.
settings.pendingIndicator: Your ERPlora account has not sent this yet: records are sealed and wait to go out.
settings.loadError: The settings could not be loaded
